display.title: Haggadah in Yiddish 2b: Slavery in Egypt and the Ten Plagues
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children on how the Jews grew into a great nation in Egypt, were enslaved, cried out to Hashem, and were taken out by Hashem Himself.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish to children, this class continues Maggid with the pesukim the Haggadah expounds. The Jews in Egypt grew into a great and mighty nation, as many as the grass of the field, and before leaving received two mitzvos connected with blood, the Korban Pesach and bris milah. Then the Egyptians made them suffer: Pharaoh feared they would side with enemies, set taskmasters over them, and made their lives bitter with mortar and bricks. The Jews cried out, and Hashem heard them, remembered His covenant with Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, and saw their suffering, including the decree to throw the baby boys into the Nile. Hashem Himself, not an angel, a seraph or a messenger, took them out. The teacher explains the five expressions: a strong hand, an outstretched arm, great awe, signs and wonders. He shows how to spill a little wine onto a broken plate at 'blood, fire and pillars of smoke', at each of the ten plagues, and at Rabbi Yehudah's signs, Detzach Adash Be'achav.
display.lesson: Hashem hears the cry of the Jewish people, and He Himself, not an angel, redeemed us from Egypt.
